audit.why: Emerald+ 52.54% over 552 games. Rumble owns levels 1-2 before Mega Adhesive exists, the mid-lane evens out, level 6 swings back to him on The Equalizer, and Rylai's onward is Singed. The chart already reads that way and it matches the Rumble-side audit in audits/top/rumble__singed.json, so I left every side and rating alone.

Levels 1-2 Flamespitter, level 3 Mega Adhesive plus Fling, level 6, Rylai's, two items — all four spikes are real and in the right order. Insanity Potion is a flat 100s at every rank, so it is a repeatable window rather than something Rumble can wait out.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built around tracking Scrap Shield — focus.text, focus.letters, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5] all name it as the matchup-defining cooldown. Scrap Shield is 6 seconds. There is nothing to bait and no window it opens. Separately, the combo that actually beats Rumble is never stated: Fling roots the target only if it lands them in Mega Adhesive.
audit.why: Riot's Fling text: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' Mega Adhesive is 17/16/15/14/13s at 1000 range; Fling is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s at 125 range. Rumble has no dash, so the grounding on Mega Adhesive does nothing to him but the root inside a live Poison Trail is lethal. The cooldowns that actually gate this lane are Flamespitter at 10/9/8/7/6s (heat-gated) and The Equalizer at 130/105/80s — a two-minute free window at rank 1.
audit.corrected: focus retargeted to The Equalizer (R), breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with Scrap Shield's 6s, Flamespitter's 10s and The Equalizer's 130s, dosFull[0] and report[5] rebuilt around the goo-then-Fling root, and content whys[2] now states the combo.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every 'trade around Scrap Shield's cooldown' line points at a 6-second ability.
audit.why: A 6s shield cannot be tracked or baited in any meaningful sense. The Equalizer at 130s rank 1 is the punishable cooldown in this lane; Flamespitter's 10s and the heat bar are the second-order tell.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0] now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Build MR' is given as a flat instruction with no mention that Electro Harpoon shreds it.
audit.why: Riot's Electro Harpoon text: it damages, slows, and reduces Magic Resist. Rumble carries 2 harpoons on a 0.5s recast, so he can strip a chunk of the MR you just bought before Flamespitter ever touches you. HP scaling is not optional here.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2] is titled 'Get caught in his Equalizer' but its body text is the generic 'turning to fight like a normal champion' boilerplate — the don't never says what to do about R.
audit.why: The Equalizer is a wall of flame, not a point. The counterplay is direction, not distance: walk perpendicular out of the band rather than along it.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Scrap Shield is 6s — nothing to bait, stop waiting on it. - Flamespitter: 10s at rank 1, and heat gates it. - The Equalizer: 130s at rank 1 — that gap is the lane. - Insanity Potion: flat 100s, kill windows only.

edits.after: Mega Adhesive and Fling are online and they are one combo: fling him into the goo and he is rooted with no dash out. Scrap Shield's 6s speed burst is his only escape, so throw the vial behind him.

notes: The mutual-displacement rule in _missing/singed.json for this pair ('Fling (E) vs Scrap Shield (W)') is a false positive — Scrap Shield is a shield plus a move-speed burst and displaces nothing; its knockup and terrain flags are tooltip-parsing misfires. The Rumble-side audit reached the same conclusion, so neither page carries that line. Mega Adhesive grounds, but grounding does nothing against Rumble because he has no dash; the value against him is the slow plus the Fling root, which is how I wrote it.
